text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The Slovak and Ukraine governments on Thursday began two-day talks on trade relations, liberalisation of trade flows and the privatisation process. Slovakia expressed strong interest in taking part in Ukraine's privatisation to ensure a larger market share for Slovak industry there, as well as in markets of other former Soviet Union states.
- Transport Minister Alexander Rezes said the motorway connecting between the capital Bratislava and borders with Ukraine should be completed within three years.

- The state Agency for Motorway Construction (SSC) said plans for highway construction this year were exceeding the production capacity of Slovak construction firms. The SSC said the main priority in motorway construction in 1997 was the south-north connection.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Finance Ministry is completing an analysis on the tax burden in Slovakia which should be used as a basis for possible amendments to the income tax law.

- Czech petrochemical firm Chemopetrol Group has opened a commercial office in Bratislava to boost trade with its Slovak partners, which accounted for about 10 percent of the group's 16 billion Czech crown turnover in 1996.

PRAVDA - The ultra-left Workers Party (ZRS), a junior member of the ruling coalition, said it would recommend citizens to vote against Slovakia's membership in NATO in the upcoming referendum on the question.
- The opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) said it would again vote for the postponement of bank privatisation.

- The National Bank of Slovakia ruled that bank Slovenska Kreditna Banka (SKB), held mainly by the countries state-owned utilities, must lower its basic capital by 237 million crowns to 673 million due to losses of 255 million crowns in 1996.

SME - ZRS said it would demand postponement of the privatisation of savings bank Slovenska Sporitelna and insurer Slovenska Poistovna, but that under certain circumstances it would not be against the privatistaion of commercial banks VUB and IRB.
